name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,406

clue.text: Backing for each swimmer in disgrace

indicators.note: backing means moving in the rear direction, so the word for each is read from its end

blocks.note: per means for each, as in ten pounds per head
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A swimmer has fallen from grace and someone is still backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: REP plus ROACH gives REPROACH; the swimmer is a fish, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Reproach as a noun is shame or discredit brought upon someone, an older sense matching disgrace.

clue.text: Care about the rise of American influence

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from bottom to top, so the word for influence runs backwards

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
drag is American slang for influence or pull

explanation.surface: Someone worries about the growth of American influence in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Care about' looks like the definition, but 'about' is the RE; drag meaning clout is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard as a noun means attention or concern given to something, so it can stand for care.

clue.text: Language used by people in Pennsylvania has a continuous trilling sound they say

indicators.note: they say means as people pronounce it, so we want a word sounding like the trill

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
a roll is a continuous trilling sound, like a drum roll

explanation.surface: Pennsylvanians speak with a rolling, trilling accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Parole here is the linguist's term, from Saussure, for language as actually spoken, as opposed to the system behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics parole is concrete speech produced by individual speakers, contrasted with langue, the abstract system.

clue.text: Interfering niece oddly neglected to pack away documents acknowledging debts

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are ignored, so only the even ones survive
packing puts something inside, so the surviving letters go between the next two pieces

blocks.note: off means away, as in going off
the second and fourth letters
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: An interfering niece forgets to put away the IOUs she holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The kept niece letters are wrapped by the words for away and debt notes together, which sit either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Officious describes someone meddlesome, overbearing in offering unwanted help or asserting petty authority.

clue.text: Charlotte races around in it

indicators.note: racing around suggests letters dashing about and ending in a new order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A well-off woman called Charlotte speeds around town in her car.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea tractor is British slang for a big 4x4 driven around posh London districts; a Charlotte is the stereotypical driver, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures an affluent woman zooming about in a large urban off-roader, the vehicle this mocking phrase names.

clue.text: Complains after time drags wearily

indicators.note: after says the complaining word is placed behind, following the abbreviation rather than leading

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to rail is to complain bitterly

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles while time drags on wearily.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail is to walk slowly and tiredly behind, pulling oneself along, so trails fits drags wearily.

clue.text: Be worthy of comparison with upcoming Irish girl

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the abbreviation runs backwards

blocks.note: Ir. is the abbreviation for Irish
Val is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Irish girl on the way up can hold her own against anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the Irish abbreviation is turned upwards; the girl's name follows it unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to rival something is to equal it or match it in quality.

clue.text: Where alcohol is found to encourage and enliven

blocks.note: first meaning, read as two words: within a strong drink such as whisky or gin
second meaning: a verb for filling someone with courage or vigour

explanation.surface: Somewhere there is alcohol that cheers people up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, IN SPIRIT; the second is one rare verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspirit is a literary verb meaning to fill with spirit, courage or life, hence hearten and animate.

clue.text: Doctor Strange concealing final piece of evidence from police officer

indicators.note: the final piece of a word is its last letter
concealing means holding something hidden within
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of evidence

explanation.surface: The Marvel hero Doctor Strange hides the last scrap of evidence from a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Strange' reads as the comic-book sorcerer, but 'Doctor' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a police rank above constable and below inspector.

clue.text: What Macbeth sees as public demonstrations of feeling

blocks.note: first meaning: the ghostly apparitions in the play, such as Banquo's ghost and the floating dagger
second meaning: open displays or expressions of emotion

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Macbeth the hero sees a dagger, Banquo's ghost and the witches' apparitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both visible appearances of spirits or ghosts and outward displays that reveal an emotion.

clue.text: Tactless remark describing Kirk essentially as an animal

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the name, its middle letters
to describe can mean to draw a line around, so the remark encircles the other piece

blocks.note: a gaffe is an embarrassing blunder of speech
the two central letters of the name

explanation.surface: Someone makes an insensitive comment comparing Captain Kirk to an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' looks like ordinary narration, but here it means drawing round, as a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is a long-necked African mammal, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Dicky raved about island fellow offering counsel

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or unsound, so the letters are in a faulty order
about means surrounding, so the scrambled word goes round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
Is. is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone named Dicky raved about an island man who gives advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but is the anagram signal; ADVER wraps IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser is a person who gives guidance or recommendations, so a man offering counsel describes one.

clue.text: An object of historical interest discovered by Catholic priest inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the priest sits within the letters for Catholic

blocks.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest unearths something of historical interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, is a crossword staple, as is RC for Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, kept for its age or associations, often in churches.

clue.text: Art class?

blocks.note: surface reading: a lesson where people learn to paint or draw
setter's reading: a category or genre of painting, one depicting motionless objects such as fruit and flowers

explanation.walkthrough: The class is not a lesson but a category of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting genre showing arranged inanimate objects such as fruit, vases and flowers is a recognised category of artwork.

clue.text: Soon returning with information on song by northern fellow in his nineties

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for soon is read from right to left

blocks.note: anon is an old word for soon
gen is British slang for information
an aria is a solo song in opera
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: An old northern man is soon back with details of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: NONA, GEN, ARIA and N run together to give NONAGENARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagenarian is someone aged between ninety and ninety-nine years old.

clue.text: Formerly a single fellow living in the centre of Cheltenham

indicators.note: the centre of a ten-letter name is its two middle letters
living in means residing within, so these pieces sit inside the town's centre

blocks.note: taken as written
the fifth and sixth letters of the ten
one means single
Tim is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: Once upon a time a bachelor lived in the middle of Cheltenham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single fellow' looks like one bachelor but splits into two pieces; Cheltenham is an English spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the past or previously, an idiomatic equivalent of formerly.

clue.text: Has a conversation about losing small pieces of sports equipment

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: to discuss is to talk something over
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Someone chats about losing bits of their sports kit.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two S's in the middle goes; 'small pieces' tempts as one phrase, but 'small' is just the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is the heavy disc thrown in athletics, so discuses are several of these throwing implements.

clue.text: Climber with backache is under a bit of pressure

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here just its first letter
in a down clue being under means placed below, so the ailment follows

blocks.note: the first letter of pressure
lumbago is pain in the lower back

explanation.surface: A mountaineer with a bad back is feeling the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is the plant: plumbago is a climbing shrub with pale blue flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago, or leadwort, is a scrambling garden shrub often trained up walls, so it counts as a climbing plant.

clue.text: Tense strikebreaker consumed by a false impression of reality for example

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so these letters go inside the false impression

blocks.note: an illusion is a deceptive appearance
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a rat is a worker who breaks a strike, a scab

explanation.surface: A tense scab worker is swallowed by a false view of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like a stock phrase, but only 'example' is the definition; 'for' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustration is an instance used to clarify or prove a point, a synonym for example.

clue.text: Sketch showing princess receiving a couple of Ephesians at court

indicators.note: a couple of means two, here the first two letters
receiving means taking in, so the princess holds the next piece

blocks.note: Di is short for Diana, Princess of Wales
the opening two letters
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A comic sketch shows a princess welcoming two Ephesians at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sketch' looks like a noun for a comedy skit, but the answer is a verb meaning to draw or portray.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict is to represent in a drawing or describe in words, which is what sketching does.

clue.text: Greek god with reportedly cool sense of smell for the most part

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so we want the spelling of a sound
for the most part means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: hip is slang for cool or fashionable
a nose for something is a sense of smell

explanation.surface: A Greek deity is said to be cool and to have a keen nose.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound is spelt with a Y as in Greek-derived words like hypnosis; the god's name gives us hypnotism.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnos is the personification of sleep in Greek mythology, twin brother of Thanatos, death.

clue.text: Sharing guilt with the Italian over getting caught tracking Communist party leader with it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
over means turned over, so the Italian article is flipped round

blocks.note: Com. is an abbreviation for Communist
the first letter of party
il is the Italian for the
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shares the blame for an Italian caught following a Communist leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tracking' means following, so the Italian and caught pieces come after the Communist and party pieces in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complicit means involved with others in wrongdoing, so bearing a share of the guilt.

clue.text: Tricked by the French mafia boss

blocks.note: le is French for the
a don is the head of a Mafia family

explanation.surface: Someone has been duped by the French mob boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to deceive or mislead them, so led on means deceived.

clue.text: Poem on breaking Freyja's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its middle letters
breaking means splitting apart, so one piece is pushed into the middle of the other

blocks.note: the two central letters of the goddess's name
the on side and leg side are the same half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A poem breaks the heart of the Norse goddess Freyja.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'on' can stand for that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem, typically a lament for someone who has died.

clue.text: No great shakes going around with this person

indicators.note: going around means encircling, so the first phrase wraps the word for with

blocks.note: so-so means middling, nothing special
and joins things, just as with does

explanation.surface: Someone mediocre is going around with a certain person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakes' tempts an anagram, but 'no great shakes' is an idiom for something only middling.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so stands in for an unnamed individual, a placeholder much like saying a certain person.

clue.text: Good to share the Head's point of view

indicators.note: to share a space means to occupy it, so the first piece sits within the next

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, meaning good
onion is British slang for the head, as in use your onion

explanation.surface: A school head's view is that good things are meant to be shared.
explanation.walkthrough: Onion for head comes from the British phrase 'use your onion', meaning think; PI for good is short for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a personal belief or judgment, the way someone sees a matter.

clue.text: Expresses disdain for southern Republican involved in fraudulent activities

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the party letter goes within the swindles

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
cons are swindles or scams
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a Southern Republican mixed up in fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: S then R inside CONS gives S-CO-R-NS.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn is to treat with contempt and open derision, so scorns means shows contempt toward.

clue.text: Answer an appeal for help to hide the finest example of banned material

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the call for help wraps the best

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
SOS is the distress signal
best means finest

explanation.surface: A response to a distress call conceals the finest instance of something prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'example of banned material', since the answer is one such substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral now prohibited in building in many countries because it causes lung disease.
